initial_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / scientific educational macro photography. IMAGE 1 IS THE EDIT TARGET: a fixed north-up top-down sequoia branchlet, field of view exactly 54.61 mm square. Keep EVERY leaf, tip, bark feature, its scale, position, colour and texture outside the two insect regions EXACTLY unchanged, same crop and camera. Add two insects physically walking ON the leaf surfaces, naturally integrated into this photograph. Image 2 is ladybug identity reference only; image 3 ant identity reference only. Do not reproduce isolated museum icons: adapt body orientation, feet/leg articulation, lighting, reflections and contact shadows to the actual leaf surface.
Ladybug: centre at EXACTLY (50%,50%) of image; overall length about 7mm = 12.8% of image width, no larger. Orange-red black-spotted shell, black/cream pronotum, six legs. Turn it naturally about 30 degrees clockwise from vertical, a slight body tilt following the sloped leaf. Feet bent and gripping leaves at different heights; some far legs partly hidden by body/foliage. Warm sun hits upper-left/west of shell, restrained asymmetric shell highlight, right side shaded green by foliage, delicate dark contact shadows immediately under feet and body plus a subtle shadow cast to the lower-right matching leaf shadows. Anatomically realistic, not perfectly symmetric.
Ant: centre at (72%,42.7%), overall span about 4mm = 7.3% of width. Small red-brown catalogue ant, six legs, angled diagonally as it climbs the neighbouring scale leaf, asymmetric planted feet and natural articulated antennae. Match same sunlight, reflected green fill and lower-right contact shadow. Both insects sharp and convincingly belonging to the same photograph. No extra insects, no dew, no text, no framing. Keep background geometry absolutely locked; any depth-of-field treatment will be applied in the viewer later. Output one square image, highest supported native resolution.
correction_prompt: Edit only the sizes of the two insects in this photo. KEEP THE LEAF BACKGROUND ABSOLUTELY UNCHANGED, same crop, every tip, veins, lighting and surface. The insects are too large. Shrink the ladybug to 55% of its CURRENT linear size (about160 pixels head-to-tail on a1254px image), centred EXACTLY at image (50%,50%), retaining its natural diagonal pose and leaf-gripping legs. Shrink the ant to35% of its CURRENT linear size (about90 pixels total length including antennae), centred at image (72%,42.7%). Reconstruct the green leaf surface where their larger versions used to be. Both insects must now be small relative to these leaves. Keep the natural left-side sunlight, asymmetrical highlights, green reflected fill and soft contact shadows in proportion to their new sizes, feet touching leaves. The ladybug should be roughly 1.75times the ant in length. Do not zoom the camera or enlarge anything else. No extra insects, no labels. Return the same square photograph.
note: Requested representative body lengths ~7mm ladybug, ~4mm ant. Poses and exact silhouettes are generated approximations, not catalogue sprites. Same fixed physical patch is used at every zoom scale. Macro focus is applied by the renderer.
